title: Subject-specific Musculoskeletal Model for Studying Bone Strain During Dynamic Motion
protocol: Take the participant to a facility with a CT scanner.
Configure the CT machine with a slice thickness of 0.625 mm, field of view of 15 cm x 15 cm, and auto settings for kVp and mAs using the machine algorithm.
Ask the participant to lie on the table that slides into the ring in the CT scanner.
Instruct the participant to remain still during the CT scan.
Scan each leg separately from the calcaneus through the distal end of the femur.
Export the CT images in DICOM format with an image size of 512 x 512 pixels (gray scale).
Measure the participant's body mass, body height, distance between anterior-superior iliac spines (ASISs), leg length, knee joint width, and ankle joint width.
Measure the linear distance between the left ASIS and right ASIS using a caliper.
Measure the linear distance from the ASIS to the medial malleolus for both legs using a tape measure.
Measure the linear distance between the lateral and medial epicondyles of the femur for both knees using a caliper.
Measure the linear distance between the lateral and medial malleoli for both legs using a caliper.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the acromion processes.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the sternoclavicular joints.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the base of the sternum.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the posterior process of the 10th thoracic vertebrae.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the anterior superior iliac spines (ASISs).
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the participant's body at the posterior-superior iliac spines (PSISs).
Place 14-mm reflective markers 1.5 cm above the lateral knee joint lines.
Place 14-mm reflective markers 1.5 cm above the medial knee joint lines.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the lateral malleoli.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the medial malleoli.
Place 14-mm reflective markers on the posterior heels.
Place 14-mm reflective markers at the bases of the second metatarsals.
Place 14-mm reflective markers at the bases of the fifth metatarsals.
Attach semi-rigid plastic plates with 4-marker clusters to the thighs.
Attach semi-rigid plastic plates with 4-marker clusters to the shanks.
Power on the motion capture system (12 high-speed infra-red cameras) and two force plates.
Open a motion capture software program.
Within the main program window, open the 'Resources' pane.
Click the "System" tab.
Configure the camera frequency at 200 Hz and force plate frequency at 2,000 Hz.
Within the main program window, open the 'Tools' pane.
Click the "System Preparation" button.
Click "Calibrate Cameras".
Click "Start".
Ask a research staff to wave a standard 5-marker calibration wand to perform a dynamic calibration within the room space where the drop-landing movements are to be performed.
Click "Stop" after 5 s of wand data have been acquired.
Place the calibration wand flat on the floor to align with a corner of a force plate for the purpose of specifying a reference location (origin) for the calibrated space.
Click "Set Volume Origin" within the 'System Preparation' tools pane.
Within the main program window, open the 'Resources' pane.
Click the "Subject" tab.
Click the "Create a new Subject from a Labeling Skeleton" button.
Select a labeling template from a list of template files provided.

In the 'properties' window, enter the subject's name and values of body mass (kg), body height (mm), inter-ASIS distance (mm), left and right leg length (mm), left and right knee width (mm), and left and right ankle width (mm).
In the 'Subject Resources' pane, right-click the subject name and click "Save Subject".
Record a static body calibration pose.

Ask the participant to stand motionless in the middle of the calibrated room with feet shoulder width apart while extending the upper extremities laterally so that all reflective markers on the body are well exposed to cameras.
In the main program window, open the Tools pane.
Click the "Subject Preparation" tab.
In the Subject Capture section, click "Start" to record a 3-s motion trial to be the static calibration trial.
Ask the participant to stand with one leg, and fully extend the other leg slightly forward.

Instruct the participant to move the extended leg around the hip joint in the following sequence: move anteriorly and return to neutral, move anterior-laterally and return to neutral, move laterally and return to neutral, move posterior-laterally and return to neutral, move posteriorly and return to neutral, and a circumduction motion.
Open the 'Tools' pane within the main program window.
Click the "Capture" tab in the 'Tools' pane.
In the Capture section, click "Start" to record a motion trial for each functional hip motion.
Ask the participant to stand with one leg and maintain a 30° hip hyper-extension of the other leg.
Instruct the participant to perform a 45° knee flexion with the non-weight bearing leg for 5 times.
Click "Start" in the 'Capture' section of the 'Tools' pane to record a motion trial for each functional knee motion.
Randomize the order of using three different drop-landing heights (26 cm, 39 cm, and 52 cm).
Place the height-adjusted wood box with a top surface area of 50 x 50 cm² on the floor covered by a rubber mat.
Ensure the wood box is 11 cm from the edges of the force plates.
Ask the participant to stand on the box surface.
Instruct the participant to extend their dominant foot directly in front of the box and shift their weight forward, then step off from the box.
Ask the participant to land with both legs on the ground simultaneously, each foot on a separate force plate.
Ask the participant to remain standing until motion capture is completed.
Repeat the motion capture three times for each height.
Open a motion capture software program.
Go to the 'Communications' pane and click "Data Management".
Select one of the recorded motion trials and open it in the program.
In the 'Tools' pane, click the "Pipeline" tab.
From the 'Current Pipeline' list, select the "Reconstruct" pipeline.
Click the "Run" button to start the reconstruction process for 3D trajectories of reflective markers.
In the 'Tools' pane, click the "Label/Edit" tab and then select individual marker names in the 'Manual Labeling' section.
Label corresponding 3D trajectories manually.
Click the "Save" button when labeling is completed.
From the 'Available Operations' list, double-click "Export C3D pipeline".
Click the "Run" button to export processed motion trial data to a file in C3D format.
Open a biomechanics software program.
Click "File" and then click the "Open/Add" button.
Select raw C3D files to import into the biomechanics software program.
From the top menu, click "Model".
Click "Create (Add Static Calibration File)".
From the sub menu, select "Hybrid Model from C3DFile".
Select and open the static calibration C3D file.
From the top menu, click "Model".
From the drop-down list, click "Apply Model Template".
Select and open a model template file.
Click the "Models" tab on the tool bar.
Click the "Subject Data / Metrics" tab.
Within the 'Subject Data' window, modify values of 'Mass' and 'Height' to make the model subject-specific.
Click the "Models" tab on the tool bar.
Click the "Model Builder Advanced Post Processing" button from the top menu bar.
In the pop-up window, click the "Functional Joints" tab.
Select "Add Motion File From Workspace".
Select functional joint center C3D files.
Highlight an imported functional joint file.
Highlight a functional joint matching the file.
Use "Set START Frame to Current Frame".
Use "Set END Frame to Current Frame".
Click the "Compute Checked Landmarks" button.
Repeat this process to calculate other functional joint centers to refine the skeletal model.
Click the "Model" button on the top menu bar.
Select "Assign Model to Motion Files".
Apply the subject-specific skeletal model to all motion trials in the pop-up window.
Click the "Pipeline" button of the tool bar.
In the "Pipeline Workshop", select the "Filtering Targets Pipeline".
Execute a fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter with cutoff frequency of 10 Hz on 3D trajectories of motion capture trials.
Click the "Pipeline" button of the tool bar again.
Select the "Filtering Forces Pipeline".
Execute a fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter with cutoff frequency of 60 Hz on ground reaction forces of motion capture trials.
Click the "Settings" button of the top menu bar.
Place check marks next to "Use Processed Analogs for Ground Reaction Force Calculations" and "Use Processed Targets for Model/Segment/LinkModelBased Items".
Click the "Pipeline" button of the tool bar once more.
Select the "Model Based Calculation Pipeline".
Execute calculations of lower-body joint kinematics and kinetics.
Click the "Pipeline" button of the tool bar.
In the pop-up window of the "Pipeline Workshop", click the "Open Pipeline" button.
Select the "Export C3D Coordinates" pipeline.
Click the "Execute Pipeline" button to export the processed 3D coordinates of lower-body visual markers in a C3D file.
Click the "Pipeline" button of the tool bar.
In the pop-up window of the "Pipeline Workshop", click the "Open Pipeline" button.
Select the "Export Ground Reaction Forces" pipeline.
Click the "Execute Pipeline" button to export the processed 3D ground reaction forces in a binary file (file extension: MAT).
Open a computer programming software.
Import the filtered C3D data file and the MAT data file.
Export a text file containing lower-body joint center coordinates.
Convert the C3D data file and the MAT data file into text files (file extension: slf) for use by a multibody dynamic simulation program.
Open the multibody dynamic simulation software program with the human body modeling plug-in installed.
Double-click the "New Model" icon within the splash screen.
Choose the generic body (GeBOD) from the drop-down list in the "Anthropometric Database Library" section.
Specify body mass, body height, gender, and age within the main modeling panel.
Click the "Lower Body" radio button within the "Body Configuration" section.
Select "Millimeter Kilogram Newton" from the "Units" drop-down list.
Click the "Apply" button in the "Create Body Measurement Table" section to accept the body measurements.
Click the "Apply" button in the "Create Human Segments" section to create a lower-body skeletal base model.
From the main menu drop-down list, select "Joints" to open the joint configuration panel.
Click the button next to "Prepare Model with Recording Joints" in the joint configuration panel.
Enter Nominal Joint Stiffness of 1 Nmm/°, Nominal Joint Damping of 0.1 Nmm∙s/°, and Joint Stop Stiffness of 3.38E7 Nmm/° in the "Spring Dampers and Joint Limits Properties" section.
Select "Left Leg" by checking the radio button next to it.
Select "Right Leg" by checking the radio button next to it.
Click the "Apply" button to accept the joint configurations.
From the drop-down list of the main menu, select "Workflow".
From the drop-down list of the sub-menu, select "Gait" and then "Calibrate".
Enter the participant's lower-body joint center file in the "Joint Center Data" section.
Click the "Load" button to import the data.
In the "Load Static Trial" section, enter the static calibration motion capture trial (in slf file format).
Click the "Load" button to import the file.
Select "Soft Tissues" from the drop-down list of the main menu.
Select "Create Base Tissue Set" from the sub-menu drop-down list.
Click "Prepare Model with Recording Muscle Elements" in the "MUSCLE CONTRACTILE ELEMENTS" section.
In the "GLOBAL RECORDING ELEMENT MUSCLE PROPERTIES" section, click the radio button for the "Updated 45 Muscle Set".
Accept default settings for muscle properties: Passive Stiffness of 0.4448 N/mm, Passive Damping of 1.75 E-2 Ns/mm, and Muscle Resting Load of 0.4448 N.
Check the radio buttons for "Left Leg" and "Right Leg" for muscle assignments.
Click the "Apply" button to accept configurations.
From the drop-down list of the main menu, select "Workflow".
From the sub-menu drop-down list, select "Gait" and "Trial".
Enter the file name of a dynamic motion capture trial (in slf file format) in the "Dynamic Trial Data" section and click the "Load" button to import the data.
Continue to enter the corresponding ground reaction force data file (in slf file format) and click the "Load" button to import the data.
From the drop-down list of the main menu, select "_Analyze".
Run the Reparameterize Analysis to adjust the model posture to match the posture in the beginning of the dynamic trial.
Open the Simulation panel.
Disable the effects of gravity and ground reaction forces.
Choose the whole motion trial as the length of the simulation.
Specify a simulation time step of 100 steps/s.
Run an inverse kinematic simulation driven by the motion capture data.
Save the inverse kinematic simulation analysis.
Open the Motion Tracker Agent Creation panel.
Accept the default tracker name: MA_Track.
Set the Translational Stiffness and Rotational Stiffness as 10 N/mm and 1,000 Nmm/°, respectively.
Set the Translational Damping and Rotational Damping as 10 Ns/mm and 1,000 Nmms/°, respectively.
Set all translational and rotational degrees of freedom as Driven.
Open an image processing program.
Import CT slices in the DICOM format.
Create a mask using the region growing method to separate bone tissue from the surrounding soft tissues.
Search for CT slices where the tibia and fibula are connected.
Erase the mask along the conjunction of the tibia and fibula bones to separate them.
Create a second mask using the region growing method to only include the tibia bone.
Go through the CT slices to uncover cavities existing in the tibia mask.
Fill the cavities in the tibia mask.
Create a 3D tibia object based on the tibia mask.
Export the 3D tibia object as a file in drawing interchange format (DXF).
Open a FE analysis software program.
Import the 3D tibia model file with the DXF extension.
Perform the Sweep command to remove duplicated elements and nodes.
Perform the Volume Mesh command to create a FE tibia model with hexagonal elements of 3 mm x 3 mm x 3 mm.
Assign Young's modulus of 17 GPa, Poisson's ratio of 0.3, and density of 1.9E-6 Kg/cm³ to all elements.
Click the "Geometry & Mesh" tab.
Select "Geometry & Mesh".
In the "Geometry & Mesh" pop-up window, in the "Mesh" section, click "Add nodes" to create two new nodes to represent the centers of the knee and ankle joints.
In the main control panel, click the "Links" tab.
Select RBE2's.
In the RBE2's pop-up window, create link connections of type 2 rigid body element (RBE2) between the joint nodes and surface nodes on the knee and ankle surfaces.
In the main control panel, click the "Boundary Conditions" tab.
In the "Boundary Conditions" section, click the "New" button.
Select "DOF_Set Nodes".
In the "Boundary Condition Properties" pop-up window, create a boundary condition by assigning six degrees of freedom to each of the two RBE2 joint nodes.
In the main control panel, click the "Loadcases" tab.
In the "Loadcases" section, click "New", select "Adams Craig-Bampton".
In the "Loadcase Properties" pop-up window, click "DOF-Set Nodes".
Select the dofset_nodes created in the above step.
In the main control panel, click the "Jobs" tab.
In the "Jobs" section, click "New".
Select "Structural".
In the "Job Properties" pop-up window, select the loadcase created in the previous step.
Click the "Job Results" button.
In the "Results" pop-up window, select "Stress" and "Strain".
Also select "Kilogram" for Mass, "Newton" for Force, "Millimeter" for Length, and "Second" for Time.
Click the "Run" button.
Click the "Submit" button in the "Run Job" pop-up window to submit the job for FE simulation and create the modal neutral file (MNF) of the tibia.
Open the post processor of the multibody simulation program.
Load the Durability plug-in program.
Open the simulation with the flexible tibia by clicking the simulation name.
Export the maximum and minimum principal strains and maximum shear strain of the nodes representing the antero-medial aspect of the mid-tibial diaphysis.
Open a computer programming software for data processing.
Import raw strain data.
Apply a fourth order low-pass Butterworth filter to the raw data with a cutoff frequency of 15 Hz.
